body:
`fractional_x_index` folds a queried longitude into `[λᵂ, λᵂ + 360)`, where λᵂ is the grid's western edge. On a `Bounded` grid covering part of the globe, that sends a longitude just *west* of the grid to the far *east* of it. The fold is also asymmetric: a node one cell east of the grid does not fold at all.

On a grid spanning 0° to 20° with two cells, halo included:

| λ | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| −15 | 35.0 | −1.0 |
| −5 | 36.0 | 0.0 |
| 5 | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| 15 | 2.0 | 2.0 |
| 25 | 3.0 | 3.0 |

Index 36 is outside the array even with halos, so interpolating a regional dataset one cell west of λ = 0 reads out of bounds — it hits a `BoundsError` under `--check-bounds=yes` and silently reads past the array otherwise.

This centres the window on the grid when longitude is not `Periodic`, so a node just outside the grid indexes just outside it. A grid spanning the full globe is unchanged in either topology, since a centred window and a west-edge window coincide there — verified for `Bounded` and `Periodic` at λ = 5, 180, 350, 357.

`Fields` 4004793 pass / 2 broken and `OutputReaders` 11549 pass, unchanged from `main`.

Includes the patch bump to v0.110.18 so the fix can be released.
title: (0.110.18) Center the longitude fold window on Bounded grids

body:
## Summary

Make `ZarrWriter` produce self-describing, CF-oriented Zarr stores that can be consumed directly by external analysis and visualization tools. xarray is used as an interoperability test, but the implementation is based on conventional Zarr/CF metadata rather than an xarray-specific API.

This also incorporates and supersedes #5718, retains this PR's grid round-trip tests and Zarr/read benchmarks, and removes substantial duplication between the Zarr and NetCDF backends.

Closes #5876.

## Zarr/CF schema

- Mark the root dataset with `Conventions = "CF-1.13"`.
- Give every root array valid, unique `_ARRAY_DIMENSIONS` metadata in reader-facing C order.
- Write one-dimensional spatial coordinate arrays at the root, named after their dimensions and annotated with CF attributes.
- Represent orthogonal spherical-shell grids with logical dimensions plus two-dimensional longitude/latitude auxiliary coordinates referenced by a space-delimited CF `coordinates` attribute.
- Physically squeeze dimensions reduced by `Nothing` locations or `Flat` topology; never emit empty or duplicate dimension names.
- Write grid metrics and immersed-boundary data while retaining private reconstruction metadata in grid subgroups.
- Consolidate metadata after initialization and every append, including distributed writes.
- Encode numeric and `DateTime` clocks with CF-compatible time units.
- Align `with_halos=false` with the `NetCDFWriter` default.
- Preserve store-aware compressor behavior for `DictStore`/S3-like stores.

## Shared writer infrastructure and cleanup

Format-independent schema construction now lives in `src/OutputWriters` and is consumed by both NetCDF and Zarr:

- dimension and coordinate discovery;
- reduced-dimension squeeze/inflate logic;
- default coordinate attributes;
- grid metrics and immersed-boundary gathering;
- field dimensions and auxiliary coordinates;
- grid reconstruction serialization.

NetCDF/Zarr extensions retain only backend storage mechanics. Relative to the merged #5718 foundation, this refactor removes 1,667 lines while adding 946 lines, a net reduction of 721 lines despite the added capability and tests.

The shared reconstruction decoder also replaces `Meta.parse` + `eval` materialization in both backends with an allowlisted parser, so reading an untrusted output store no longer evaluates arbitrary Julia code.

## Round trips and compatibility

- `FieldTimeSeries` round trips work for rectilinear, stretched, latitude/longitude, orthogonal spherical-shell, and immersed-boundary grids covered by the suite.
- Reduced fields round trip for any squeeze pattern, including `Average(c, dims=(1, 2))`.
- The reader accepts both the new squeezed representation and reduced fields written unsqueezed by current `main`.
- Multiple grids use collision-free dimension, coordinate, metric, and reconstruction names.

### Metadata compatibility

This PR corrects a long-standing LatitudeLongitudeGrid metadata typo in both writer backends: meridional angular-spacing variables are now named `Δφ_afa` and `Δφ_aca`, rather than the misleading `Δλ_afa` and `Δλ_aca`. Consumers that access those two variables by name must update accordingly.

## Validation

- Julia acceptance harness: 15/15 writes and `FieldTimeSeries` round trips pass for regular, reduced, stretched, and latitude/longitude cases.
- Legacy-store compatibility: reduced `T̄z` and `T̄xy` fields written by current `main` load successfully with the new reader.
- External acceptance harness: all 371 checks pass independently on both zarr-python 2.18.7 and 3.3.0, including `xarray.open_zarr`, lazy Dask reads, coordinate promotion, `.sel`, labeled reductions, reduced fields, and consolidated metadata.
- `test/test_zarr_writer.jl`: construction, raw values, `DateTime`, reductions, functions, windowed averages, reconstruction, multi-grid, append/restart, alternate stores, grid-type sweep, and Tripolar cases pass locally.
- Targeted NetCDF writer/reader and reconstruction cases pass after the shared-layer refactor.
- ExplicitImports checks pass for `OutputWriters` and both extensions.

## Benchmarking

The existing additions in this PR remain: Zarr write benchmarks, directory-store size and chunk reporting, and read-mode benchmarks across Zarr, JLD2, and NetCDF.

## Related work

- Incorporates and supersedes #5718.
- Builds on the cross-writer round-trip coverage from #5654.
- Addresses the missing Zarr grid-coordinate behavior described in #5639.
title: Make Zarr output CF interoperable; expand tests and benchmarks
